sections.name: When Heroin Was Cough Medicine

lines.prompt: A cosy 1900s pharmacy with wooden shelves, a pharmacist in a waistcoat handing a small brown bottle to a mother holding a coughing child

lines: In 1898, a German company started selling a brand new cough medicine. It was called Heroin.

lines.prompt: Close-up of an old brown glass medicine bottle with a cork on a wooden counter, warm lamp light

lines: Bayer named it heroin, from the German word for heroic, because it was meant to be so powerful.

lines.prompt: A 1900s doctor in a waistcoat listening to a patient's chest with a stethoscope, the patient coughing

lines: It really did calm coughs, at a time when diseases like tuberculosis were common.

lines.prompt: A pharmacist in 1900s clothes holding a bottle and a morphine bottle side by side, looking proud

lines: It was even sold as a safer, less addictive alternative to morphine.

lines.prompt: A doctor in 1910s clothing frowning at a stack of patient files, a worried patient shaking in the background

lines: Within a few years, doctors noticed patients becoming badly addicted.

lines.prompt: A 1920s government official locking a cabinet of medicine bottles with a big key

lines: In the US, heroin was banned completely in 1924. Bayer's other new drug from that time did better. Aspirin.
